paragraphs.text: Halifax JB789 of 1658 Heavy Conversion Unit was on a circuits and landings exercise from Riccall. It took off for its third circuit at 01.00 and struck the spire of St James Church, Selby, at 01.02 on 10 May 1944. It came down across Portholme Road and Union Lane, through the roof of Portholme Mill and onto Portholme Drive. All seven aircrew were killed. The inquiry reached no firm conclusion. The sources give different totals for civilian dead, so the number is not settled here.

A metal plaque on the nave wall at St James Church, Selby, records the strike and the church's restoration, and is shown with British and Australian flags and the spire's cockerel. Yorkshire Aircraft says a memorial plaque was unveiled in the church on 1 November 1953 and that a 70th anniversary service was held there in 2014. The church was re-dedicated on 11 December 1950 and the tower was rebuilt without a spire.
The church website refers to a WWII display in the church.

notes: DUPLICATE VERDICT: SAME memorial and same aircraft. Correct serial is JB789 (1658 HCU, Riccall). (1) Yorkshire Aircraft traces JB789 from 158 Sqn to 1658 HCU and the 10 May 1944 Selby spire strike (two pages). (2) IWM 30919, titled JB798, describes one plaque in St James Church recording a 10 May 1944 RAF aeroplane striking the spire; no source shows a second Selby memorial or a second Halifax. (3) JB798 was a different airframe: IBCC puts JB798 (78 Sqn, EY-P, Fraser) on the Hamburg raid of 30 July 1943, crashed at Bad Oldesloe, crew buried Hamburg. The seven crew names in our JB798 record (Fraser, Nicholls, Hetherington, Baillie, Goodacre, Campbell, Woodcock) are that 1943 crew, not the Selby crew; IWM's inscription text as we hold it appears to carry them too. The Selby crew per Yorkshire Aircraft are Laver, McDermott, Rockingham, Storer, Knight, Roper, Dixon. Caveat: coordinates differ by about 200 m (53.784012,-1.068781 vs 53.782467,-1.071457; the IWM grid SE 61280 32193 is the plaque position); both are inside the one church area, and the 1953 plaque date (Yorkshire Aircraft) vs a plaque mentioning 1950 re-dedication (IWM) could mean two plaques, not checked. Our JB789 record's 9 May 1944 date is unsupported: both IWM and Yorkshire Aircraft say 10 May. Recommend merging the JB798 record into JB789 after human review. CUSTODIAN: not found. No source says who looks after the plaque. IWM 30919 names no maintainer; the church site (S4, S7) does not mention it beyond a 'WWII display'. The memorial is inside the Church of England parish church of St James, so the church (vicar and PCC) is the obvious enquiry point, but that is an inference, not sourced; nothing found for Selby Town Council, RBL or a local society. The 2014 Press article cited by Wikipedia could not be read and may name a parish contact. Also doubtful: our record's 'original cockerel weather vane' and 'seven civilians' wording is not supported by what was read (IWM says 8 civilians commemorated; Yorkshire Aircraft implies 15 dead in total; church says 6 residents). Note IWM text says the cockerel was found under debris. Sources S1 and S4/S7 are independent of S2. The Facebook source in our record was not used.
